capabilities: Highlight hard-to-read sentences, adverbs, passive verbs, hedges and complex words as you type
Explain a highlight on click and fix it with one-click suggestions or a permanent ignore list
Show grade, word count, reading time and per-problem counts in a side panel
Rewrite and proofread text with an optional locally downloaded AI model
Set writing goals for a note or day with a streak counter
disambiguation: Unofficial reimplementation of the Hemingway Editor's feedback inside Obsidian; it is not affiliated with hemingwayapp.com and says it is not a replacement for the paid app.
extras: The optional AI feature downloads a ~2.3 GB Llama 3.2 model once and needs WebGPU (recent desktop Obsidian); it runs fully offline. The README notes its grade matched the Hemingway website on one test note but its self-written word lists can differ. Installable via BRAT (dhruvir-zala/hemingway-for-obsidian).
intentEvidence: Not affiliated with Hemingway Editor. This is an independent, unofficial, community-made plugin.
motivation: The author used the Hemingway app daily but kept their notes in Obsidian, and got tired of copying text out and back in a browser tab.
problem: Obsidian gives no readability feedback, so writers copy text out to the Hemingway app in a browser and paste it back.

relations.evidence: Not affiliated with Hemingway Editor. This is an independent, unofficial, community-made plugin.

summary: Hemingway-style readability feedback that highlights hard-to-read sentences and wordy words live, with grade stats and optional on-device AI rewriting.
